newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Glassmaker Glaverbel surges in Brussels.
newsitem.headline: Glassmaker Glaverbel surges in Brussels.

text.p: Belgian glassmaker Glaverbel rose five percent to 4,200 francs in early trading on the Brussels bourse on Friday after reporting better-than-expected annual results late on Thursday.
Group net profit more than doubled in 1996, boosted by extraordinaries, with better operating results seen in 1997.
Group net profit rose to 1.768 billion francs from 621 million in 1995, after extraordinary profit of 606 million.
This included a net capital gain of 1.166 billion francs from the sale of Glaverbel's stake in U.S. glass group AFG Industries.
Glaverbel is controlled by Japan's Asahi Glass Co Ltd.
"The results were not wonderful but they were a lot better than analysts' forecasts," said one trader.
"They had some bright elements in them, particularly the fact that the sale of AFG improves the structure of the balance sheet. There has been a cut in fiancial charges," he added.
"All in all the sentiment is friendly after the figures," another trader said.
The strong gain in the Glaverbel shares ran counter to the overall market with was tending flat to lower after the overnight 58-point decline of the Dow Jones.
